questions.question:
In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.

When I was at school I found my class teacher to be the best mentor as she always have time to listen and guide.

options.text: as she always have time to listen and guide

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2) i.e., 'as she always have time to listen and guide**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part **as she always have time to listen and guide.**
 
• The given sentence is in **past tense **as it talks about the time when the subject was in school. (was, found are past tense verbs)
 
• But in **option 3 **the **present tense verb have** has been used. 
 
• This makes **as she always have time to listen and guide **the incorrect part. 
 
• Thus, **option 3 **is the correct answer. 

So the correct sentence is- When I was at school I found my class teacher to be the best mentor as **she always had time to listen and guide.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• We can correct the part **as she always have time to listen and guide **by using **had instead of have. **

questions.question:
**In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The teacher and her student was engaged in a discussion on the current political crisis.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e., 'was engaged'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The error lies in the part **'was enagaged'** in the given sentence. 
 
• **Teacher **and **student **are two **subjects **joined by **and. **
 
• If the subject consists of two or more words that are connected by and then **the subject is plural.**
 
• To maintain the **subject-verb agreement, **plural subjects need a plural verb. 
 
• **Was engaged **is incorrect as **was **is a **singular verb. **
 
• Thus, **option 3 **is the correct answer. 

So the correct sentence is- The teacher and her student were engaged in a discussion on the current political crisis

• **abandon - **cease to support or look after (someone); desert.
 
• **introduce - **bring (something, especially a product, measure, or concept) into use or operation for the first time.
 
• **amend - **make minor changes to (a text, piece of legislation, etc.) in order to make it fairer or more accurate, or to reflect changing circumstances.
 
• **initiate - **cause (a process or action) to begin.
 
 
 
• **​**The given blank needs a word that would signify the step taken by the states with respect to existing labour laws following the migrant crisis. 
 
• From the above meanings it is clear that **amend **is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. 
 
• So, **option 3 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order.

A. How will we ever reach our goal if we don't follow our ideals and principles and follow the path we say we believe in?

B. Many of us believe in God, do our daily prayers and vow to be good.

C. But unfortunately, when it comes to putting our ideas into practice, we procrastinate.

D. There may be variations in our chosen ideals of Him, but each of us believes in Him nevertheless.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3) i.e., 'BDCA'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• When arranging sentences, it is easier to order the first few; and then eliminate the options accordingly. 
 
• The first sentence of a paragraph is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 
 
• Here, only B is independent and introduces the topic which deals with the belief in God and how that believe is expressed through prayers and vows. 
 
• So, B becomes the first sentence of the passage. 
 
• Both options 1 and 3 show sentence B as the first sentence. 
 
• So, we need to find the second sentence which will be either sentence A or D.
 
• Sentence A questions about the path that can be taken to reach our goals. But we need a mention of these goals first, before a question regarding them can be put forth. 
 
• So, sentence D which talks about how there are variations and different paths to reach or believe in God, occupies the **second position. **
 
• So, D must come after B. Then BD is the correct order.
 
• As per **option 3,** the full sequence is : BDCA.
 
 
• 
 
**B.** Many of us believe in God, do our daily prayers and vow to be good.

 
 
• 
 
**D.** There may be variations in our chosen ideals of Him, but each of us believes in Him nevertheless.

 
 
• 
 
**C.** But unfortunately, when it comes to putting our ideas into practice, we procrastinate.

 
 
• 
 
A. How will we ever reach our goal if we don't follow our ideals and principles and follow the path we say we believe in?

 
 
 
 
• 
 
This sequence is logically correct, making option 3 the correct answer.

questions.question:
Examine the four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. Yet few people know the long history of making soap.

B. As a prevention, they recommend the frequent washing of hands for 20 seconds.

C. Scientists have declared that COVID-19 is here to stay.

D. This advice is practical and easy to follow as soap is a common and inexpensive consumer product.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1) i.e., 'CBDA'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When arranging sentences, it is easier to order the first few; and then eliminate the options accordingly. 
 
• The first sentence of a paragraph is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it. 
 
• Here, **only C is independent** and introduces the topic which deals with a declaration made by scientists regarding a disease. 
 
• So, **C** becomes the **first sentence** of the passage. 
 
• Both **options 1 **and **2** show **sentence C** as the first sentence. 
 
• So, we need to find the **second sentence** which will be either **sentence A or B.**
 
• **Sentence A** talks about how few people know the long history of soap making. This sentence does not provide more information on sentence C. So, it cannot occupy the second position. 
 
• But **sentence B** talks about how (they) are recommending frequent hand washes as a prevention measure. This links sentence B to sentence C which had talked about a disease. Logically a disease needs to be prevented. 
 
• So, **B must come after C**. Then** CB is the correct order.**
 
• As per option 1, the full sequence is : CBDA.
 
 
• 
 
**C. **Scientists have declared that COVID-19 is here to stay.

 
 
• 
 
**B.** As a prevention, they recommend the frequent washing of hands for 20 seconds.

 
 
• 
 
**D.** This advice is practical and easy to follow as soap is a common and inexpensive consumer product.

 
 
• 
 
**A.** Yet few people know the long history of making soap.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
This sequence is logically correct, making option 1 the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.

The miscreants were shifted to another building that same evening and __was keeping__ in custody by the police.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1) i.e., 'were kept'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The underlined part of the given sentence is incorrect as **was keeping **is the **past continuous tense form **of the verb **keep. **
 
• The given sentence is in **simple past tense form **and so the past continuous tense form cannot be used. 
 
• The **simple past tense form of keep is kept. **
 
• We need to use the **linking verb were** as the sentence deals with the **third person plural** (*they for the miscreants → (they) were kept*).
 
• So, **option 1 **is the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

**So the correct sentence is-** *The miscreants were shifted to another building that same evening and** were kept** in custody by the police.*

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

"Madam, please watch this program on our folk songs," says Sitab.

options.text: Sitab asks Madam have you watched the program on their folk songs.
Sitab said to Madam to watch the program on our folk songs.
Sitab says Madam is watching the program on our folk songs.
Sitab requests Madam to watch that program on their folk songs.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 4) i.e., '****Sitab requests Madam to watch that program on their folk songs.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is a form of **imperative sentence **where a request has been made by using the word **please. **
 
• We need to follow the steps to change an imperative sentence to indirect speech - 
 
 
• The **reporting verb says** is changed into **requests.**
 
• Put **that** between the reporting and reported speeches.
 
• The **first person our** will be changed into **their.**
 
• The tense of the given sentence is **present tense (watch) **which remains unchanged in the indirect sentence. 
 
• The **verb to** is added before the verb of the reported speech (**watch**). 
 
 
 
• Eventually, we will get the final sentence- Sitab requests Madam to watch that program on their folk songs.
